title: Recent advances in luminescent lanthanide based Single-Molecule Magnets
claim: An applied magnetic field can Zeeman-split or shift Ln3+ emission lines of SMMs, providing an independent check of the lowest mJ gaps, but intensity changes are expected to be weak because the magnetic field has even parity under Judd–Ofelt selection rules.
explanation: For the Cs–Dy beta-diketonate complex, pulsed fields up to 36 T at 5 K map the splitting of the ground mJ = ±15/2 and first excited mJ = ±13/2 doublets and confirm a gap of about 100 cm−1. The D5h cyclohexyl(diphenyl)phosphine-oxide Dy complex shows field-induced shifts and asymmetric band overlaps consistent with close first and second excited states. The same Zeeman response can occur in ordinary paramagnetic Ln complexes, so it is not by itself proof of SMM–luminescence synergy.
scope: Luminescent Dy3+ SMMs studied under static or pulsed magnetic fields.
conditions: Low temperature (example at 5 K) and high pulsed fields (up to 36 T in the cited Cs–Dy study).
caveats: Field-dependent spectra may not resolve every zero-field component. True synergy with superparamagnetic coercivity below the blocking temperature had not been shown.
